text:
jess: Heads up — I spotted a ~12% dip in prefix cache hit-rate for model-mosaic-v2 on /summarize starting 03/12 after the kernel-2.1.3 rollout. Token-saved metric dropped too.

matt: ugh. can you paste the dashboard slice? is it per-route or global? :eyes:

jess: link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abc123/prefix-hitmap?panel=7 (panel filtered to model=mosaic-v2, route=/summarize). Looks per-route and concentrated in high-qps customers.

sasha: did we change batching heuristics or kernel selection logic in that deploy? kernel bump also landed the new dynamic-kernel-selector A/B.

jess: yes — rollout changed preferred kernel to avx-fused for sequence_len<1024. suspect kernel runtime differences altered batching latencies and cache key alignment (we saw more split prefixes).

ana: infra-bot: Deploy 2026-03-12T08:41:22 -> kernel-2.1.3 rolled to 60% canary.

leo: quick probe: ran this PromQL against prefix_cache: sum by(route,model,customer) (rate(prefix_cache_hits[5m])) / sum by(route,model,customer) (rate(prefix_cache_requests[5m])) -> shows hit-rate down from 0.78 -> 0.66 for /summarize.

matt: can you grab a sample of keys that missed and compare raw fingerprint lengths? might be a key-normalization/serialization edge after kernel switch.

jess: pasted a small sample below (sanitized):

```
missed_keys_sample = [
  "mosaic-v2:/summarize:ctx=chat:v=1:pref=hash_0x8f4a",
  "mosaic-v2:/summarize:ctx=chat:v=1:pref=hash_0x2d11",
  "mosaic-v2:/summarize:ctx=chat:v=1:pref=hash_0x9b00"
]
```

jess: noticing more variation in prefix canonicalization — some keys include trailing metadata that used to be normalized away.

sasha: that smells like a serializer change in the runtime path used by avx-fused. I remember a micro-optimization flattened metadata into the prefix buffer to avoid copies.

matt: related perf regression: increased 95p latency for small inputs by ~10ms which would reduce batching effectiveness and increase KV misses. we should compare KV serialization outputs between kernels.

jess: action: I'll run a small A/B replay locally — replay 1k /summarize requests with kernel=old vs kernel=2.1.3 and diff keys.

ana: infra-bot: scheduled replay job job-id=pf-replay-232 at 2026-03-12T10:00 (assigned to jess).

leo: meanwhile I'll add a temporary dashboard with these panels: per-route hit-rate, token-saved delta, per-customer top-10 miss contributors, kernel-by-hit-rate heatmap. quick Grafana query snippets below:

```
# per-route hit rate
sum by(route) (increase(prefix_cache_hits[30m])) / sum by(route) (increase(prefix_cache_requests[30m]))

# token saved delta vs baseline
sum by(route) (increase(tokens_saved[30m])) - sum by(route) (increase(tokens_saved_baseline[30m]))
```

matt: please also add a panel that breaks out by kernel_tag so we can see which kernel variant correlates with misses.

sasha: if serializer change is confirmed, revert that micro-optimization or add a normalization step before keying. normalization is cheap compared to token cost.

jess: preliminary replay results: 2.1.3 produced 9% more unique keys for same input set. attached diff shows extra metadata bytes inserted before the prefix hash.

matt: ok -> rollback plan? can we hotfix kernel selector to prefer generic-kernel for /summarize until a proper fix lands?

leo: yes we can push a routing override: route->kernel map in config-store. I'll prepare a canary to set /summarize -> generic-kernel for customers in tier=prod.

ana: infra-bot: config-change proposed: /summarize -> generic-kernel (canary 20%). Approve? :white_check_mark:

jess: approved. after rollback I'll re-run token-saved comparison and update the dashboard.

matt: follow-ups: (1) add unit test to catch key-serializer regressions (2) add a histogram for key-length pre/post kernel selection (3) add alert if per-route token_saved drops by >5% vs rolling baseline.

sasha: will pick up serializer test. jess will own replay and dashboard. leo will do routing override. matt will own alert and rollback.

jess: thanks team. logging the actionable items in the ticket: https://linear.redwood/internal/INF-4523 (prefetch hit-rate kernel-drift).

leo: small note — add customer slices by traffic-shape; we saw one large customer driving most of the delta. might be a tenancy-specific keying bug.

jess: ack. will include per-customer diffs in the ticket and tag eng-sre for deeper infra profiling if needed. :thumbsup:
